answer: Each agent must burn a unique basalt token tied to its hardware kernel to register, making identity cloning expensive. A periodic beacon broadcasts a random challenge; agents answer using their kernel-keyed signature, and peers verify under 3 seconds. Duplicate registrations fail because the basalt token is single-use and burned on-chain. An attacker needs one physical device plus a burned token per sybil identity, so mass fake accounts cost linearly more than honest participation, capping the attack at the price of hardware.
